summary: Specifies a certificate extension for carrying Network Function Types (NFTypes) of the 5G system in X.509 v3 public key certificates, profiled as in RFC 5280. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Parts of a 5G network have different jobs. This lets a digital ID card say which job its owner does, so others can tell what role it has.

questions: what is the x.509 nftype extension
how do 5g network functions identify their type in certificates
can the nftypes extension be critical
subtitle: A certificate extension that lists which 5G network function types a certificate holder serves.

tldr.problem: In a 5G System, certificates identify interface instances of network functions, but the subject name and SubjectAltName only support identity-based access control, not decisions based on the role a function plays.
tldr.mechanism: The NFTypes extension, identified by id-pe-nftype, holds a sorted list of one or more short ASCII Network Function Type strings, such as AMF, inside an X.509 v3 certificate.
tldr.outcome: Operators of 5G Systems can make role-based access control decisions from certificates. The strings must be unique, since the same string used by two operators for different roles could cause confusion or wrong decisions.

today: RFC 9310 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2023, and the unit metadata shows no RFC obsoleting or updating it. The text notes that the extension can be used by operators of 5G Systems or later.

sections.title: Why Certificates Need a Role
sections.content:
The 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) specifies several Network Functions (NFs) as part of the service-based architecture of the 5G System. There are 56 NF Types defined for 3GPP Release 17, each identified by a short ASCII string. They are listed in Table 6.1.6.3.3-1 of 3GPP TS 29.510.

Operators of 5G Systems use an internal PKI to identify interface instances in the NFs. They use X.509 v3 certificates (RFC 5280), whose primary function is to bind a public key to the identity of the certificate subject. The subject and the SubjectAltName extension support identity-based access control.

This RFC adds the NFTypes extension to support role-based access control by listing the NF Types associated with the subject. It can be used by operators of 5G Systems or later.
sections.eli5: A certificate is like an ID card that says who you are. This adds a line saying what your job is, so the network can decide what you are allowed to do.

sections.title: The NFTypes Extension
sections.content:
The NFTypes extension MAY be included in public key certificates. It is identified by the object identifier id-pe-nftype, which is { pkix id-pe(1) 34 }, that is 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.1.34. The extension MUST NOT be marked critical.

Its syntax is a sequence of one or more NFType values, and each NFType is an IA5String of 1 to 32 characters.
sections.eli5: The extension is a small list tucked inside the certificate. Each item on the list is a short code word naming one kind of job.

sections.title: Rules for the NFType Strings
sections.content:
The RFC sets several requirements on the list:

  • It MUST contain at least one NFType.
  • Each NFType MUST contain only ASCII, with at least one and at most 32 characters. It MUST NOT include control characters (values 0 through 31), the space character (value 32) or the delete character (value 127).
  • The same NFType MUST NOT appear more than once.
  • If there is more than one NFType, they MUST appear in ascending lexicographic order using the ASCII values.

IA5String is used so the underscore character, which is not part of PrintableString, can appear in names.
sections.eli5: The list has house rules: no empty entries, no repeats, no spaces, and the entries must be in alphabetical order.

sections.title: The ASN.1 Module
sections.content:
Section 4 gives the formal ASN.1 module NFTypeCertExtn, following the conventions of RFC 5912 and RFC 6268. It imports the EXTENSION class from the PKIX common types module, defines ext-NFType with the syntax NFTypes identified by id-pe-nftype, and gives the module identifier number 106 under id-mod.

Appendix A lists the strings from Table 6.1.6.3.3-1 of TS 29.510 for 3GPP Release 17, such as AMF, SMF, UPF, AUSF and NRF. The list is not exhaustive.
sections.eli5: The ASN.1 module is the exact blueprint that computers use to read and write the list, so every system builds it the same way.

sections.title: The Example Certificate
sections.content: Appendix B shows a certificate that follows the profile in Table 6.1.3c.3-1 of TS 33.310. It carries an NFTypes extension with a single NFType, AMF. Its SubjectAltName extension holds a fully qualified domain name and a uniformResourceIdentifier carrying the NF Instance ID. The appendix gives the PEM text and a decoded ASN.1 dump in which the extension appears with the OID 1 3 6 1 5 5 7 1 34.
sections.eli5: The example is a real-looking ID card with one job written on it, 'AMF', along with the name and number of the machine that owns it.

sections.title: Security and Privacy Considerations
sections.content:
The security considerations of RFC 5280 apply. Some NF Type strings are standard, and an operator MAY assign its own for use in its network. Because the NF Type drives role-based access control, an operator-assigned value MUST NOT overlap with a value in the commonly defined set. Two operators using the same string for different roles could cause confusion or incorrect access control decisions. How to check uniqueness across operators is outside the scope of the RFC. Operators may also need different levels of confidence that NFTypes were properly assigned, so they might have different trust models for the extension.

On privacy, certificates are sent in the clear in some protocols such as TLS 1.2 (RFC 5246) but are encrypted in others such as TLS 1.3 (RFC 8446). With plaintext certificates, the extension can help an observer identify which systems are of most interest.
sections.eli5: Two companies must not use the same code word for different jobs, or someone could be let into a room by mistake. Also, an ID card shown in public tells watchers what job its owner has.

sections.title: IANA Actions
sections.content: IANA has assigned an object identifier for the certificate extension, allocated in the "SMI Security for PKIX Certificate Extension" registry (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.1). IANA has also assigned an OID for the ASN.1 module identifier, allocated in the "SMI Security for PKIX Module Identifier" registry (1.3.6.1.5.5.7.0).
sections.eli5: A librarian reserved two official numbers so nobody else can use them: one for the extension and one for its blueprint.

data.title: ASN.1 syntax
data.code:
NFTypes ::= SEQUENCE SIZE (1..MAX) OF NFType

NFType ::= IA5String (SIZE (1..32))
